note: 40 verified rooms, the densest of the fourteen. 27 of them stand in Midtown between 34th and 58th Street, with a second cluster in the Financial District and the Village. Cote is counted here as a Korean beef room and overlaps the korean_bbq corpus; Task 3 counts it once and must not import the Koreatown grill census wholesale. Also carries the note folding in the six Bronx rooms.

19 verified rooms in four clusters: Williamsburg (4, including Peter Luger), the Midwood and Borough Park kosher steakhouse belt (6), Bay Ridge (3) and Downtown Brooklyn (2). The kosher belt is the borough's second real cluster and appears in no mainstream best-of list.

16 verified rooms, and the borough's steakhouse is South American rather than prime beef. 9 of the 16 sit on the Argentine and Brazilian parrilla belt along Northern Boulevard, Roosevelt Avenue and Queens Boulevard through Jackson Heights, Elmhurst and Corona; Astoria adds two Greek-American steakhouses, with outliers in Bayside, Forest Hills, Flushing and South Ozone Park.

6 verified rooms against a bar of 8, which is what decided it. The borough does have a nameable cluster — Jake's, Arnauld's and Riverdale Steak House are all in Riverdale, 3 of the 6 — so it fails on count, not on shape. The rest are scattered across Throgs Neck and Parkchester, and NYY Steak and Lobel's fail the venue-embedded test. Folded into a note on the Manhattan page.

4 verified rooms against a bar of 8, and unlike the Bronx there is no cluster either: Tompkinsville, St. George, South Beach and Bulls Head, one room each. Two opened in the last four years and none has verifiable history; Raval's own marketing calls it the island's only authentic steakhouse. This path does not exist in destination_tree.json and, because the city is dropped, no node needs to be added.

37 verified rooms, nine of them in the World's 101 Best Steak Restaurants 2026. The core is Mayfair, Soho and the City, but Hawksmoor's seven sites, Gaucho's four and Blacklock's four spread the corpus across the boroughs.

21 verified rooms, every one inside the city limits, and unlike korean_bbq no suburban split. Korean BBQ's mass fled Lawrence Avenue for Niles and Glenview; the steakhouse mass never left River North, the Gold Coast, the Loop and the West Loop. Suburban Gibsons Oak Brook and Rosemont are not needed.

24 verified rooms. The page covers three municipalities: 15 in the City of Los Angeles from Koreatown and Downtown out to Echo Park, Hollywood, Venice and the Valley, 7 in Beverly Hills and 2 in West Hollywood. No split, because the City of Los Angeles sustains a page on its own. Following korean_bbq's puget-sound.json, the guide sits on this node while each room carries the node it is actually in, so Task 3 must create united-states/california/beverly-hills and united-states/california/west-hollywood.

13 verified rooms, all inside the city, and unlike korean_bbq no South Bay page pulling the mass south. Clusters: Nob Hill's Van Ness spine, the Financial District and Embarcadero, and the Design District and Jackson Square, with Marina, Cow Hollow and the Mission behind them.

22 verified rooms, all inside the city limits, so the page is Seattle and not Puget Sound. This is the sharpest inversion of korean_bbq, whose Seattle guide had to become a regional page because the grills were four suburban corridors up to forty miles out. Steak concentrates in the downtown and Belltown business core, with Capitol Hill, Ballard, Queen Anne and the lake neighborhoods behind it; Bellevue's John Howie Steak is not needed.
12 verified rooms in two clusters, 6 in Back Bay along Boylston, Berkeley and Arlington, and 4 in the Seaport, with Beacon Hill and Downtown Crossing between them.

17 verified rooms, and the page is the District only, not the District plus Northern Virginia. The same rule as Seattle decides it: measure inside the limits first and extend only if the core cannot sustain a page. It can, on the K Street power-dining corridor with a second node in Georgetown. Northern Virginia's Tysons and Arlington chain corridor is dense enough to be its own page one day but is not one of the fourteen candidates.

7 verified rooms against a bar of 8. The correction that moved it: The Ruxton opened in March 2024 in the former Fleming's space at 720 Aliceanna Street, and the first pass counted both as separate rooms. Same address, successive tenants, one room. Dropped rather than merged into Washington DC, because a merge puts the rooms on the target page and Baltimore City rooms on a page named Washington DC would misname it across a state line and forty miles, contradicting the District-only ruling on that row.

20 verified rooms across four municipalities rather than a split: 9 in Miami proper in Brickell, the Design District, Little River, Little Havana, Little Haiti and Downtown, 8 in Miami Beach where South of Fifth carries the spectacle rooms, 2 in Coral Gables and 1 in Aventura. Kept as one page because Miami proper sustains a page on its own and the city's own tourism board publishes a single steakhouse list spanning all four. Following korean_bbq's puget-sound.json, Task 3 must create united-states/florida/miami-beach, united-states/florida/coral-gables and united-states/florida/aventura.
